crop_profile.summary: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a globally important annual cereal grown on loamy to clay soils with pH 6.0-7.5. Optimal temperatures are 10-25 °C, rainfall 300-900 mm/year, and sunlight 6-10 h/day. It requires medium water and nitrogen, with critical moisture needs during flowering. Major producers include China, India, Russia, the United States, and France. Typical yields are 3 t/ha, reaching up to 7 t/ha under optimal management. Key diseases are Fusarium head blight, powdery mildew, and leaf rust; main pests include aphids, Hessian fly, and wheat midge. Integrated pest management, split nitrogen fertilization, and timely harvest ensure high quality grain.

Apply a mulch layer (straw, rice hulls, or biodegradable film) immediately after each irrigation to reduce evaporation and improve soil temperature.
Within 3 days, apply a balanced nitrogen fertilizer (e.g., urea 50 kg ha⁻¹) to exploit the existing high nitrogen status and promote rapid vegetative recovery.
Within 7 days, incorporate compost or well‑rotted organic manure (≈10 t ha⁻¹) to increase soil organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity.
Adjust irrigation schedule to maintain consistent soil moisture during the upcoming flowering stage (critical water‑requirement period).
Conduct weekly visual scouting for Fusarium head blight and powdery mildew; if symptoms appear, apply the recommended fungicide promptly.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will halt the current vegetation decline, allowing the wheat to resume normal growth, achieve near‑optimal yields, and maintain profitability despite the heat stress episode.
monitoring_plan: Daily: Record soil moisture at 0‑30 cm depth using a portable sensor; adjust irrigation as needed.
Weekly: Obtain NDVI and NDWI from satellite or drone imagery; target NDVI >0.45 and NDWI >0.1.
Continuous: Log ambient temperature and humidity; alert if temperature stays >28 °C for >3 consecutive days.
Weekly: Inspect canopy for disease symptoms; document any incidence and treatment actions.
At flowering (day 60‑70): Verify that soil moisture remains ≥70 % of field capacity and that nitrogen levels are adequate via leaf tissue test.
